claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Are you currently living in the UK yourself?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're both here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. You and Alex both live together in Manchester.

Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and expenses (such as food, clothes, and other living costs)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - I look after Alex every day and pay for everything they need - food, clothes, school things, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's very helpful. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following situations:**
- In hospital or residential accommodation for an extended period?
- Living in care provided by the local council?
- Living with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. Alex lives at home with me full-time - not in hospital, not in care, just living here with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually there is a bit of a situation there. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for Alex, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. We're both involved in looking after Alex, but we haven't sorted out between us who should be the one to claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail.

According to the Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. When two people are both responsible for a child and cannot agree on who should claim, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will make the decision about who will receive the Child Benefit.

Let me ask: **Do you and Alex's other parent both live with Alex, or does Alex live primarily with you while the other parent contributes to their upkeep or shares care in another arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me - they don't live with their other parent. We both contribute to Alex's care, but Alex's home is here with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's helpful to understand the situation.

Since Alex lives with you full-time and you're providing their day-to-day care and covering their expenses, you would typically be the person who claims Child Benefit. However, because you mentioned that you and Alex's other parent cannot agree on who should claim it, this creates a specific situation.

Let me ask one more question to complete the assessment:

**Has either you or Alex's other parent already submitted a claim for Child Benefit for Alex to HMRC?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us has submitted a claim yet. That's partly why we haven't been able to sort out the disagreement - we're trying to figure out who should actually make the claim.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: ELIGIBLE

Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)  
✓ Alex lives with you in the UK  
✓ You are responsible for Alex's day-to-day care  
✓ You pay for Alex's expenses (food, clothes, school items, etc.)  
✓ Alex is not in hospital, care, or living elsewhere  

### About the disagreement with Alex's other parent:

The fact that you and Alex's other parent disagree about who should claim doesn't make you ineligible. Here's what you should know:

- **Only one person can claim Child Benefit for Alex** - not both of you
- Since Alex lives with you full-time and you provide the day-to-day care, you would typically be the appropriate person to claim
- Ideally, you and Alex's other parent should try to reach an agreement about who will claim
- If you cannot agree and both of you were to submit claims, HMRC would decide who receives the benefit

### What to do next:

Since neither of you has claimed yet, you can go ahead and make a claim for Child Benefit. However, I'd recommend trying to reach an agreement with Alex's other parent first to avoid any complications. If that's not possible, you can still proceed with your claim, and HMRC will handle any disputes if they arise.

Would you like information on how to make a claim?
